title: Biggest and smallest in one walk
idea: TOOL: track a running max AND a running min at the same time - two comparisons per turn.

exercises.prompt: You want the HIGHEST and the LOWEST score from a list in one pass. How many trackers do you keep?
options: Two - one holding the biggest so far, one the smallest so far
exercises.explanation: One tracker per fact: a 'biggest so far' and a 'smallest so far'. Each turn you check both.
high rises 40, 70, stays 70; low falls 40, stays, then 20. Final: 70 and 20.

exercises.prompt: Why start 'low' at a very BIG number like 1000 before the loop?
options: So the first real score is smaller and replaces it
exercises.explanation: A high starting value guarantees the first real score is less, so low snaps to a real value. (Starting low at 0 would be wrong - nothing is below 0.)

exercises.prompt: Tracking the biggest is the same pattern as tracking the smallest, just with the comparison flipped.
exercises.explanation: True. 'If bigger, keep it' becomes 'if smaller, keep it'. Same shape, opposite comparison.
You keep s when it is LESS than the smallest so far, so the test is s < low. Output: 2.

exercises.prompt: Arrange a loop that finds the biggest and smallest of [8, 3, 6].
exercises.explanation: Start high low and low high, test each item against both, then print. Output: 8 3.

exercises.prompt: A subtle bug: a learner starts BOTH high and low at 0 for the list [5, 2, 9]. What goes wrong?
options: low stays 0 - nothing in the list is below 0, so it never updates
exercises.explanation: low at 0 is already smaller than every positive score, so it never changes. Starting values for min/max matter.
With one item, both trackers snap to it: high 50, low 50. A single value is both the biggest and the smallest.

exercises.prompt: Both 'if' checks for high and low can live in the same loop turn.
exercises.explanation: True. Each turn you run both tests on the same item n. Two trackers, two checks, one pass.

options: Max and min are twin trackers - run both each turn in one pass
You need two loops for two results
exercises.explanation: Biggest and smallest are mirror-image trackers. Keeping both in one walk is multiple state in action.
